article._excerpt: Award-winning documentary on 2018 northern B.C. wildfires coming to Williams Lake | Williams Lake Tribune Award-winning documentary on 2018 northern B.C. wildfires coming to Williams Lake The Fire In Our Hearts, an award-winning wildfire documentary, is coming to Williams Lake on Nov. 7 and Nov. 12 at Paradise CInemas. As wildfires raged in 2018 forcing his friends, family and neighbours to choose to evacuate or remain to protect the land that defines them filmmaker Josias Tschanz knew he wanted to give his remote community in northern B.C. a voice. Tschanz is bringing his feature length award-winning documentary that he hopes will spark discussion, The Fire In Our Hearts, to Williams Lake on Saturday, Nov. 7 and Thursday, Nov. 12. The film follows communities located directly south of Francois Lake and tells the story of ordinary residents, First Nations and firefighters who chose flight over flight.. “At first it was not a film,” Tschanz said noting, he immigrated to Canada when he was 16 years old from Switzerland and his parents live in the area. At the time of the fires that resulted in ferry access being restricted, Tschanz was smuggled through the toxic smoke on a shipping boat with a friend. “It was just to document things and then create a GoFundMe page, and we had a video that would help people that had lost a lot in the community, but then what happened was the beautiful story of the community coming together and forming an organization.” That organization, Tschanz, said is the Chinook Emergency Response Society which is now a national blueprint on how smaller communities can be part of the solution when there is wildfire and they are too remote to access and provide resources and time. This is where the story takes off, according to Tschanz, telling more than just the fires themselves but the aftermath and what happened during that time. article.title: [americanagnetwork.com] USDA moves nearly $4 million to expand Kansas meat processing
article.content_html:
🪶 ✏️

The U.S. Department of Agriculture is moving forward with nearly $4 million in grants to 10 Kansas meat processors to expand capacity and give livestock producers more local processing options. The funding is part of a $57.4 million round covering 147 awards in 40 states through the Meat and Poultry Processing Expansion Program. USDA said it can begin obligating the grants after completing the congressional notification period. The largest Kansas grant, $2 million for Plainview Beef Company in Peabody, will help renovate and equip a processing facility, including cold storage, packaging, rendering and wastewater systems. USDA says the projects aim to expand market access for independent producers and increase competition among processors. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said, “A strong, independent processing sector is essential to our food security, and these Kansas processors build the resilient supply chain this country needs”.

article._excerpt: The U.S. Department of Agriculture is moving forward with nearly $4 million in grants to 10 Kansas meat processors to expand capacity and give livestock producers more local processing options. The funding is part of a $57.4 million round covering 147 awards in 40 states through the Meat and Poultry Processing Expansion Program. USDA said it can begin obligating the grants after completing the congressional notification period (americanagnetwork.com, meatingplace.com). The largest Kansas grant, $2 million for Plainview Beef Company in Peabody, will help renovate and equip a processing facility, including cold storage, packaging, rendering and wastewater systems. USDA says the projects aim to expand market access for independent producers and increase competition among processors. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said, “A strong, independent processing sector is essential to our food security, and these Kansas processors build the resilient supply chain this country needs” (americanagnetwork.com, beefmagazine.com). Capacity targets: Kansas grants are projected to raise Hat Creek Butchery’s daily harvest capacity by 200%, Walnut Valley Packing’s processing capacity by about 140%, Randel’s annual capacity by about 67% and T & W Meat’s annual capacity by about 25% (americanagnetwork.com, beefmagazine.com). Other states: The round includes $2.17 million for two Iowa facilities, about $1.1 million for six Illinois projects and $1.07 million for four Wisconsin processors (meatingplace.com). Nebraska award: Wahoo Locker in Nebraska will receive $250,000 for automated packaging equipment for pork and beef products (klkntv.com, meatingplace.com). Program scale: USDA says it has awarded more than $200 million to independent processors through the program since it began (meatingplace.com, americanagnetwork.com).
